title: The second and third time
hookLine: going once, going twice: some things only settle on the third
tomorrow: a rule you give yourself: is it still a rule?

cards: Nobody at an auction thinks the first call is enough, and nobody needs it explained: some things only settle on the third. The refuges work in threes too.
After the first round, the chant starts again with one new word, dutiyampi, a second time, and then tatiyampi, a third time. So, yesterday's question: why not once?

teach.b: Honest answer first: the chant itself never says why. It just does it. Dutiyampi Buddham saranam gacchami: a second time, to the Buddha I go for refuge.
Then the dhamma, then the sangha. Then tatiyampi, and all three again.
Notice that each round names all three refuges; the three times aren't one per jewel.

teach.h: IN THE VINAYA: HOW ONE WENT FORTH.
teach.b: Where the texts do show the threefold saying at work is the Vinaya, the monks' rule. There, the Buddha allows a newcomer to go forth by saying the refuges this way, three times through.
Said once, it's a line. Said three times, in front of others, it marks a real step, like the third call at an auction.
And for anyone just learning there is a plainer gift: by the third round, the words come without looking at the sheet.
So the second and third time aren't filler. They're how the words become a decision. A second time, a third.

how: In Theravada temples the refuges are chanted three times through, with dutiyampi and tatiyampi opening the second and third rounds, usually right after the homage.

games.q: what does “the second and third time” mean?
o: the names of two early monks in the canon
a pause the chanters take for breath
the words that open rounds two and three

games.q: the week in Pali — tap the pairs.

s: the chant explains why the refuges are said three times
it doesn't. the Vinaya shows the threefold saying as the way a newcomer went forth.
each of the three rounds names just one refuge
each round names all three: the Buddha, the dhamma and the sangha.

games.q: at an evening chant, the person beside you loses the place right after namo tassa. what comes next?
games.why: the homage finishes first: to the Blessed One, the worthy one, the one fully awake. the refuges, three times through, come after.

practice: Chant the refuges three times through, as slowly as you like: Buddham, dhammam, sangham saranam gacchami, then dutiyampi, then tatiyampi.
When the third round ends, keep still and listen to the last sound of your own voice fading, all the way to the quiet underneath it.

wordCard.voice: The second and third time. Dutiyampi, tatiyampi: the words that turn one saying of the refuges into three. Word nine of a little Pali.

orig.note: dutiyampi, tatiyampi in Devanagari letters: a second time, a third time.

carryVoice: The line for this one: a second time, a third, and the words become a step. A week and a day of Pali.
